newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Council of Europe calls for end to Albania violence.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe calls for end to Albania violence.

text.p: A Council of Europe mission on Friday welcomed Albania's decision to halt a military advance against rebels in the south and called on all political parties to condemn insurgents who ignored an arms amnesty.

In a statement issued at the end of two days of talks with government and opposition leaders, the four-member team called on the main opposition Socialist Party to take up parliamentary seats it won in a disputed general election last year.

"We warmly welcome the declaration of March 6...on the need for restoring constitutional order, for an amnesty in return for surrender of arms and for multi-party consensus on the choice of a new prime minister," the statement said.
"All political parties should state their condemnation of acts of criminal violence and rebellion in southern Albania if these should persist despite the March 6 offer of an amnesty."

President Sali Berisha ordered a halt to the army's push on Thursday after a meeting between his ruling Democratic Party and opposition groups. Forces had been moving south since Monday under emergency rule introduced in response to insurgence in several southern towns.

"We call on the people of Albania to accept and act in accordance with this amnesty. The logic of these developments is for the Socialist Party to end its boycott of parliament: only thus can its voice be heard and its arguments debated in the parliamentary assembly of the council of Europe," the statement said.

Albania is a member of the 40-state Council of Europe, set up to promote democracy and human rights. The mission urged the government to respect the European Human Rights Convention and end restrictions on domestic media.
Rene van der Linden, Dutch vice president of the Council of Europe parliamentary assembly and leader of the team, said the mission had held a 90-minute meeting with Berisha.

Berisha had underlined that he was committed to a peaceful solution to the two-month crisis in Albania but repeated that he would not bow to opposition demands to form a coalition government with the Socialists, reformed heirs to the Communist Party. He also repeated he saw no room in the short-term for fresh elections.
The Council of Europe mission called for the drawing up of a rescue package by international financial institutions and offered to facilitate further dialogue between Albania's political parties.
